subject.title: [Bug]: Agents should not be able to access or modify files outside their own working space.

question: Should OpenClaw make per-agent workspace confinement the default boundary for host file tools, and what scope should be promised for exec and sandboxed tool execution?
rationale: This choice changes a public security boundary and compatibility posture: current docs/tests preserve unrestricted host file access by default, while the user report shows real workspace corruption risk.

options.title: Define a maintainer-approved confinement contract
options.body: Choose the default, upgrade guidance, and explicit exec scope before merging PathGuard, relative traversal, or workspaceOnly-default changes.

options.title: Land a file-tool-only boundary with explicit limits
options.body: Accept a narrower read/write/edit/apply_patch policy only if docs and labels clearly state that shell-mediated access remains separate.

options.title: Keep unrestricted host tools as the supported default
options.body: Close or downgrade this only if maintainers decide sandboxing and tools.fs.workspaceOnly are sufficient opt-in controls for this class of report.

recommendation.title: Define a maintainer-approved confinement contract
recommendation.body: Choose the default, upgrade guidance, and explicit exec scope before merging PathGuard, relative traversal, or workspaceOnly-default changes.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest history on the filesystem policy guard and current review context for this security/default tradeoff.
